children.text:
Handover... a word I never really thought would hold any significance in my life.

If you don't know what I'm talking about, handover is a special service at our school where the former church committee passes down its responsibilities to the new one. The girls dress up
mu mishanana

, the boys in their suits looking all clean, and honestly, it is always such a beautiful thing to witness. For the longest time though, it felt like something meant for other people, never me.

Me? Shy me? Weird me? Sinful me? Imperfect me?

Why was
I

chosen?

Me, a leader in the church? Much less
grand-mere wa

church? Never in my deepest thoughts, and no, I am not exaggerating.

Then one normal afternoon, during one of our exhausting or should I say, mind-boggling classes, the names were announced. The shock on my face probably said everything before I even could. Even afterward, it still did not feel real. Some things happen so unexpectedly that your mind takes time to catch up.

And sooner or later, handover was here.

As we danced into church that Sunday, I felt excitement, fear, gratitude, and disbelief all at once. I remembered how years ago I had been pushed into doing modern dance during one of our church services despite my seriously terrible history of dancing. But somehow, little by little, God kept pulling me out of places I thought I would stay in forever.

Sitting there that afternoon, I became hyperaware of myself. Too much excitement felt like pride. Too little would make me look ungrateful. But somewhere in the middle of all my overthinking, I remembered something simple: this was never a performance for people. It was all for God alone.

Then someone I genuinely consider my spiritual role model, shared the Word of God with us. Out of everything he said, one thing that I still remember is that: we must truly understand who we are praying to, the weight of His glory, the depth of His power, and pray in accordance with that. Amen.

He also reminded us that as leaders, we are called to be examples to the church. That the church here was now in our hands.

At that point, ironically... my hands literally started shaking.

Afterward, the former
grand-pere & grand-mere

shared their final words as leaders before giving my partner and me hugs and handshakes. And later on, they laid down a mat, and as the new committee, we knelt while the entire church prayed over us. All I could think of was how great our God is.

While praying, I suddenly remembered this exact season last year during the farewell service for our candidates. Everyone around me was joyful, but inside, it felt like chains were binding me. I knew exactly why. I knew what I had done, and I knew the Lord had seen it, yet I still tried to ignore it.

I prayed once. Then again. Then several more times. But it felt like my prayers were not even going past the bridges of my mouth. I felt so guilty before God, and all I could do was sit before Him. In that moment, forgiveness felt impossible.

But surely, His grace truly is, and always will be sufficient for me.

Through repentance, prayer, and a real change of heart, the Lord pulled me out of that dark place. I repented for days, even months... and well, the rest is history really.
Amateka yange yarahindutse.

So as I knelt there surrounded by prayers, I thanked God for delivering me from that place. And I reminded myself that the same God who carried me through such a low valley is the same God who will walk with me throughout this new journey in the committee.

And additionally, as that same someone wrote to us:
Ubushake bwawe n' umuhate bubanza mbere yo gushobozwa n' Uwiteka.

So in many ways, it still comes down to the posture of my heart, not only during my time as a leader, but for the rest of my life.

And over that, I pray in Jesus' name. Amen.

That's all, be blessed!
Le 10.05.26

There’s this song called Faithful in All of Your Ways.
I don’t really go searching for it. It really just shuffles its way back to my playlist.

There’s a part in it I’ve always known. It was never something I paid special attention to, just a line that existed in the song. It goes: “I love You, Jesus, I worship and adore You, just wanna tell You that I love You more than anything.”
This time, I found myself singing it like I always do.
But somewhere in repeating it, it stopped feeling like just words I knew… and started feeling like something I was actually saying. Like a prayer.
And I couldn’t just brush past that.

Because I struggle with prayer. With communication. With feeling like I’m truly in fellowship with God. I speak, and I know He hears me. I know He speaks too. But I can’t hear Him, and that’s something I’ve been trying to figure out for a while now.
So I started wondering.
Have I ever really told Him I love Him?
Not in passing. Not because it fits into how things are supposed to sound. Not in front of people. Just… to Him.
And if I haven’t, then what has all of this been?

We’re made in His image. And I know how deeply us people want to be loved. Not watched. Not performed for. Loved. And when I think about Scripture saying He’s jealous for us, I can’t help but see it through that lens. Like He wants something real from me too.
So now I’m here, sitting with a question I didn’t expect to ask.
Have I been loving Him at all? If any, more than anything?

I read something earlier that said the longer you stay on the wrong train, the harder and more expensive it is to return to where you were meant to go. It doesn’t answer this, but it makes it harder to ignore. It makes me take this seriously instead of brushing past it.

Because it’s easy to keep going and call it consistency.
Easy to justify instead of being honest.
But I don’t want to do that.
If I’m off track, I want to know. Even if it costs me the comfort I’ve been sitting in.

I don’t have an answer. Not yet.
I’m just leaving this here for the version of me that will.
For now, all I know is this:
those words didn’t feel empty when I said them, and I want to love Him more than anything.
I love You Abba.

posts.title: Faithful In All Of Your Ways

children.text: At the beginning of my second term, our school dropped an unexpected announcement: no classes for three days. Naturally, excitement filled the air. But when we asked why, the answer felt… off, they said:
“abakobwa bazahugurwa”
(girls will be trained).
Trained? That word didn’t sit right with me.

I was curious, slightly skeptical, but we weren’t given much more information. Time passed, and I almost forgot about it, until one of our teachers brought it up again. What started as a complaint about the boys in class took a turn I didn’t expect. He spoke about how, yes, they can be disobedient, inattentive even - but they’re building things, coding, chasing ideas, trying to make something of themselves. Then… he compared them to us.
He said we, the girls, follow instructions, get top grades… but that’s it. That our potential just sits, unused.
Then he said something that, I can’t lie, really shocked me:
“Nshaka ko namwe mukubagana.”
“I want you to be stubborn too.”
I never thought such words would come from a teacher.
By the time the “trainings” arrived, I wasn’t exactly excited, but I was definitely paying attention. All the girls were grouped randomly into classrooms. That’s where we met our facilitators from
Resonate Workshop
Ms. Nyinawumuntu and Ms. Ghislaine.
What happened over the next three days is honestly hard to fully explain - but I’ll try.

We weren’t taught that we could code too. We weren’t told we were “better than boys.” Instead, we were asked to think deeply. To resonate with ourselves. About leadership. About identity. About responsibility.

We talked about what it actually means to be a leader: not a title, but someone who takes initiative to solve real problems. “Umuyobozi ni umuntu ufata iya mbere… “ Nyinawumuntu said. At the time, I was part of the school committee at the time, nearing the end of my mandate. and for the first time, I questioned whether I had truly
led
We revisited
indangagaciro z’ Umunyarwanda,
values I had memorized long ago but never really
lived
“gukunda umurimo,” “kwiyemeza,” “kwihesha agaciro.”
They stopped feeling like lyrics… and started feeling like standards.
Then came the reflections.

At one point, we were given a drawing of a tree: roots, stem, branches, fruits. It sounds simple, but it was one of the most honest conversations I’ve ever had with myself. Who am I, actually? What grounds me? What am I growing into?
And throughout it all, they listened. Really listened. They created a space where we could speak freely, question norms, and challenge what we had quietly accepted.

Why do we let boys dominate, almost all, spaces?
Why do teachers move on after asking just a few students, usually boys, if they understand?
Aren’t we all capable? Didn’t we all earn our place here?

By the last day, we were asked to set our own goals. Now, I’ve never been great at that, in fact I’ve been more than horrible. I’ve always seen goal-setting as something that sounds good but rarely sticks. But this time wasn’t the same.
After those three days, I felt accountable, not just to the facilitators, not just to the program, but to myself. To the girl I had spent those days rediscovering.
So I wrote my goals with intention. Not to keep them trapped on paper, but to live them. To see them through, in the light of day and even in the uncertainty of night.
And just like that, it ended.

Unironically, life didn’t suddenly transform overnight. But it’s something within me, that shifted. I carried a quiet confidence, a clearer sense of purpose. Small changes, but meaningful ones. And over time, those small shifts started creating bigger outcomes.

Even now, months later, I might forget the exact lessons. I might forget certain moments. But I will never forget the girl I reconnected with during those few days, the one I had somehow lost along the way.
And for that, I’m grateful. I thank you God, for all you do, has a reason.
Tukamushimiraa 🤏🏽

That’s all for today.
Love you & stay positive 💛
There’s been opportunities that’ve been coming my way sometimes that make me pause.

Not because I don’t want them.
But because a small voice in my head begins listing all the reasons I shouldn’t have them.

Maybe someone else deserves it more.
Maybe someone else would do it better.
Maybe I’m not ready yet.
Maybe it’s simply too big for me.
And before I even try, I begin shrinking myself to fit the version of the world where those things are true.

Today I heard someone speak about experiencing that same feeling. The same quiet doubt that appears when something meaningful is placed in your hands. But they spoke about a small shift they had made.

They said the feeling doesn’t always go away. Sometimes it still shows up, whispering the same old things. But instead of stepping aside like they had before, they chose to remain where the opportunity had found them.
And that small decision stayed with me.

Maybe opportunities don’t come because we are perfectly ready.
Maybe they come because we are meant to grow into them.
And maybe the only thing we really have to do is stay where we are… long enough to try.
So when the next door opens, I hope I remember this small decision.
Not to shrink.
That was me. 12.03.26

Today reminded me about patience.

The day started with me being given a punishment for waking up late💀 to arrange firewood. What's worse than a punishment, is one that's unnecessary!
By the time I got to class, they were already saying the closing prayer. Oddly, that bothered me more than it should have, and I could feel myself starting to think the entire day was off to a rough start.

But I stopped myself there. Instead of holding on to that feeling, I chose to be grateful that I even made it in time to say the prayer.

Not long after, our teacher came in to return our exam papers. I xould swear my heart stopped beating for a second when he began projecting some of our answers onto the tv to "showcase" our mistakes. At one point, he took a picture of mine, just as I expected.

The results weren’t exactly what I hoped for, especially in a subject that matters to me and almost entirely connects to what I want to pursue in the future. For a moment it stung. But I remembered something I had read the day before: “Until death, all defeat is psychological.”

As dark as it may sound, it's what helped me let it go & continue on with my day.

Later in the evening, while I was working on something, my Spotify shuffled to a random song called “I’ll Never Tell” by Luke Chiang. The very first words of it were: “Patience. All of this will make sense.”

I was humbled..

I’ve come to realize many times that God’s plan is incredibly detailed, even in the small setbacks that frustrate me along the way. As the scripture says in Jeremiah 29:11, only He knows the plans He has for us; plan for us to prosper and not to harm us.

By the end of the day, I felt a quiet sense of calm and awareness settle in. A reminder that everything is still unfolding the way it should.

And because of that, I simply continued with my day; patiently.

posts.title: Doesn't it all happen for a reason?

children.text: There are many things I have wanted to do. Planned to do, even. I would get excited just thinking about them, sometimes even overwhelmed by the amount of ideas sitting in my head.

But most of the time, they stayed there. Just possibilities of what could be.
Which eventually led me to ask myself a simple question. Why?

When I was little, I used to journal. I had what felt like a million diaries, and for some reason they were always the brightest colors. Pink, orange, anything that would stand out amongst any other books. I would write in them what I believed were my deepest, darkest secrets😂. When I finished a page, I would let out a lil’ sigh like I was the main character in my own one-woman series.
But that episode ended the day one of my classmates got hold of one of those diaries. That moment engraved a lesson in me about people. Not everyone deserves access to your inner world.

For a while after that, I kept most of my thoughts to myself. I wrote everything in my mind instead. I would speak to myself, answer myself, and carry my thoughts quietly. Looking back, that was probably the quietest I'd ever been.
At the time I thought I was simply protecting my privacy. What I did not realize was that little by little, I was also feeding another habit. Overthinking.
Eventually I tried to get out of my own head by opening up to the people closest to me. I shared my feelings more freely and, in a way, they became my journal. It helped. It still does sometimes.

Now, at 17, I realize that for the longest time that was my way of escaping my thoughts. What I failed to see was that all those moments where I felt like I needed somewhere to pour everything out, I could have spoken to God. Instead, I chose something as trivial as a book or another person.
I have come to that realization more than once. Each time thinking that simply realizing it was enough to change something. Yet somehow I would fall back into the same habits again and again.

As I said, I’m the kind of person who reaches an understanding and believes that is where the work ends. For a long time, I never actually did anything about the things I realized. I only thought about them.

Another thing about me is that I forget easily. I can promise God that I will talk to Him more and somehow still drift away from that promise. Someone could hurt my feelings deeply and before long I find myself treating them like my closest friend again. I can even make promises to myself over and over without ever really holding myself to them.
So because of that, I decided to make this little thing you are reading right now.

Somewhere my thoughts can live outside of my head without feeling exposed. Somewhere I can return to, write, adjust, build on, and slowly shape over time. In a way, it lets me clear my mind while also creating something I genuinely enjoy working on.

More than anything though, it quietly keeps track of the things I do not want to forget. The promises I have made to myself and to God, the goals I want to grow into, and the memories that deserve to stay longer.
And with that, I mean, this is where it begins.

That will be all for today, 09.03.2026.
(I promise the readings will be shorter… or even longer next time😊)
Jah Bless.
